title: A power series ring over a Noetherian N-2 domain is a Noetherian N-2 domain
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] integral domain which is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], and let $R[[x]]$ be the ring of formal power series in one variable $x$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] (the case $n=1$). Then $R[[x]]$ is a Noetherian integral domain and $R[[x]]$ is N-2: for every finite field extension $L$ [def-pc-field-extension] of the fraction field of $R[[x]]$, the integral closure of $R[[x]]$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $R[[x]]$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032Q (lemma-power-series-over-N-2, lines 45592-45609), statement ('If R is Noetherian, a domain, and N-2, then so is R[[x]]') and proof (Lemma Noetherian-power-series, Lemma power-series-over-Noetherian-normal-domain, Lemma 032P tate-japanese, Lemma 032K finite-extension-N-2)

proof.text: *$R[[x]]$ is a Noetherian domain.* By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-noetherian] (with $n=1$) $R[[x]]$ is Noetherian, since $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-domain] (with $d=1$) $R[[x]]$ is an integral domain, since $R$ is. This proves the first two assertions; it remains to show that $R[[x]]$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032Q (lemma-power-series-over-N-2), proof, first sentence ('Observe that $R[[x]]$ is Noetherian by Lemma Noetherian-power-series'); the domain clause of the statement

proof.text: *The normalization $R'$ of $R$.* Let $K$ be the fraction field of $R$ and $R'\subseteq K$ the integral closure of $R$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Taking $L=K$ in the definition of N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], $R'$ is a finitely generated $R$-module, generated by $r_1,\dots,r_m$ say. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] (with $A=R$, $L=K$) $R'$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] with fraction field $K$; by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] it is Noetherian; and by [lem-weil-pbc-n2-ascends-finite-domain-extension] (with $A=R\subseteq B=R'$, $R'$ finite over $R$, $R$ Noetherian and N-2) $R'$ is N-2.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032Q (lemma-power-series-over-N-2), proof, second and third sentences ('Let $R'\supset R$ be the integral closure of $R$ in its fraction field. Because $R$ is N-2 this is finite over $R$'); that $R'$ is Noetherian and N-2, used for Tate's lemma, is left implicit there

proof.text: *$R'[[x]]$ is finite over $R[[x]]$.* Since $R\subseteq R'$, the ring $R[[x]]$ is the subring of $R'[[x]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] of series with all coefficients in $R$; $R'[[x]]$ is an integral domain by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-domain], so $R[[x]]\subseteq R'[[x]]$ is an extension of domains. It is generated as an $R[[x]]$-module by $r_1,\dots,r_m$ (step 2): for $f=\sum_{k\ge0}a_kx^k\in R'[[x]]$ choose for every $k$ elements $c_{k1},\dots,c_{km}\in R$ with $a_k=\sum_jc_{kj}r_j$; then, comparing coefficients, $f=\sum_{j=1}^mr_j\,g_j$ with $g_j=\sum_kc_{kj}x^k\in R[[x]]$. So $R'[[x]]$ is a finitely generated $R[[x]]$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032Q (lemma-power-series-over-N-2), proof, fourth sentence ('Hence $R'[[x]]$ is finite over $R[[x]]$')

proof.text: *$R'[[x]]$ is a Noetherian normal domain.* $R'$ is a Noetherian normal domain (step 2), so by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-normal-domain] $R'[[x]]$ is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032Q (lemma-power-series-over-N-2), proof, fifth sentence ('By Lemma power-series-over-Noetherian-normal-domain (Tag 0BI0) we see that $R'[[x]]$ is a normal domain')

proof.text: *$R'[[x]]$ is N-2 by Tate's lemma.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tate-n2-complete-principal] to the ring $R'[[x]]$ and the element $x$: (1) $R'[[x]]$ is a Noetherian normal domain (step 4); (2) by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-quotient-variables] (with $A=R'$, $d=i=1$) the constant coefficient map $R'[[x]]\to R'$ is a surjective ring homomorphism with kernel $xR'[[x]]$, so $R'[[x]]/xR'[[x]]\cong R'$, which is an integral domain and N-2 by step 2 (both properties pass along a ring isomorphism, which identifies the fraction fields and the integral closures in each finite extension); (3) by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-variables-complete] (with $A=R'$, $d=1$, $I=(x)=xR'[[x]]$) $R'[[x]]$ is $xR'[[x]]$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Hence $R'[[x]]$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032Q (lemma-power-series-over-N-2), proof, sixth sentence ('Apply Lemma tate-japanese (Tag 032P) to the element $x\in R'[[x]]$ to see that $R'[[x]]$ is N-2'); the hypotheses (2) and (3) of 032P, which the source leaves to the reader, are written out

proof.text: *Descent to $R[[x]]$.* $R[[x]]\subseteq R'[[x]]$ is an extension of integral domains with $R[[x]]$ Noetherian (step 1) and $R'[[x]]$ a finitely generated $R[[x]]$-module (step 3), and $R'[[x]]$ is N-2 (step 5). By [lem-weil-pbc-n2-descends-finite-domain-extension] $R[[x]]$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. With step 1 this proves the lemma.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032Q (lemma-power-series-over-N-2), proof, last sentence ('Then Lemma finite-extension-N-2 (Tag 032K) shows that $R[[x]]$ is N-2')
